measurements.name: Height
measurements.why: Helps the drafting tool check that your lengths make sense together.
how: Stand barefoot against a wall, heels touching it.
Lay a book flat on your head, against the wall, and mark under it.
Measure from the floor to the mark.

measurements.name: Full bust or chest
measurements.why: The main measurement for choosing a top or dress size, and for drafting a bodice.
how: Wear the underwear you'd wear with the garment.
Wrap the tape around the fullest part of your chest, under your arms and across your shoulder blades.
Check in a mirror that it's level all the way around.
Breathe normally and read the tape where it meets, snug but not tight.
measurements.tip: Snug means the tape touches all the way around without pressing in. Patterns add the extra room (called ease) for you.

measurements.name: High bust
measurements.why: If this is 2 in (5 cm) or more smaller than your full bust, it helps pick a size that fits your shoulders. You'll use it in levels 4 and 6.
how: Wrap the tape high under your armpits, above the fullest part of the chest.
Keep it high across your back too.
Read it snug, not tight.

measurements.name: Underbust
measurements.why: Useful for fitted tops, empire waists, and bodice drafting.
how: Wrap the tape around your rib cage, right under the bust.
Keep it level and snug.

measurements.name: Natural waist
measurements.why: Used for skirts, pants, and dresses, and as the reference line for many other measurements.
how: Tie a piece of elastic or string around your middle.
Bend side to side a few times. It settles at your natural waist, usually the narrowest spot, a little above your belly button.
Measure along the elastic, snug but not tight. Leave the elastic on for the next measurements.
measurements.tip: This is usually higher than where you wear jeans. Measure the natural waist anyway: patterns are drafted from it.

measurements.name: High hip
measurements.why: Helps fit the area just below the waist, around the tummy and hip bones.
how: Measure about 3 to 4 in (8 to 10 cm) below your waist elastic, around your hip bones.
Keep it level.

measurements.name: Full hip
measurements.why: The main measurement for choosing a skirt or pants size, and for drafting.
how: Stand with your feet together.
Wrap the tape around the fullest part of your seat, usually 7 to 9 in (18 to 23 cm) below the waist.
Look in a mirror from the side to keep it level, and slide it up and down to find the fullest spot.

measurements.name: Neck
measurements.why: Used for collars and necklines.
how: Wrap the tape around the base of your neck, where a shirt collar would sit.
Keep it snug, without adding a finger of room: the pattern adds ease.

measurements.name: Upper arm
measurements.why: Makes sure sleeves aren't too tight.
how: Let your arm hang relaxed.
Measure around the fullest part of your upper arm.

measurements.name: Wrist
measurements.why: Used for cuffs and sleeve ends.
how: Measure around your wrist bone.

measurements.name: Thigh
measurements.why: Used for pants and fitted skirts.
how: Stand with your weight on both feet.
Measure around the fullest part of one thigh, near the top.

measurements.name: Shoulder length
measurements.why: Sets the length of the shoulder seam.
how: Find the side of your neck, where a necklace chain sits.
Find your shoulder point: the bony tip at the edge of your shoulder. Lift your arm and feel for the dip; it's just above it.
Measure between the two.

measurements.name: Across back
measurements.why: Gives your back and shoulders room to move.
how: Stand relaxed with arms down. A helper makes this easier.
Find the creases where your arms meet your back, about 4 to 5 in (10 to 13 cm) below the bump at the base of your neck.
Measure straight across between the creases.

measurements.name: Across front
measurements.why: Helps fit the upper chest.
how: Find the creases where your arms meet your chest, about 3 in (8 cm) below the base of your neck.
Measure straight across between them.

measurements.name: Back waist length
measurements.why: Sets the length of a bodice back. Very important for drafting.
how: Tip your head forward and find the bump at the base of your neck (the nape bone).
Stand straight again. Measure from that bone down your spine to the waist elastic.
A helper makes this much easier.

measurements.name: Front waist length
measurements.why: Sets the length of a bodice front, including room over the bust.
how: Start at the side of your neck, where a necklace chain sits.
Measure down over the fullest point of your chest, then straight down to the waist elastic.

measurements.name: Shoulder to bust point
measurements.why: Places bust darts at the right height.
how: From the side of your neck, measure down to the fullest point of your chest (the bust point).

measurements.name: Bust point to bust point
measurements.why: Places bust darts the right distance apart.
how: Measure straight across from one bust point to the other.

measurements.name: Arm length
measurements.why: Sets sleeve length.
how: Bend your elbow slightly and rest your hand on your hip.
Measure from your shoulder point, over the elbow, down to the wrist bone.

measurements.name: Waist to hip
measurements.why: Tells the pattern where your hips are widest.
how: Measure down the side of your body from the waist elastic to the level of your full hip.

measurements.name: Waist to knee
measurements.why: Handy for skirt and short lengths.
how: Measure down the side from the waist elastic to the middle of your knee.

measurements.name: Waist to floor
measurements.why: Sets full pants length (also called the outseam).
how: Stand barefoot.
Measure down the side from the waist elastic straight to the floor.

measurements.name: Inseam
measurements.why: The inside leg length of pants.
how: Stand barefoot with feet slightly apart.
Measure from the crotch straight down the inside of your leg to the floor.
Easier: measure the inside leg seam of pants that fit you well, and add how much longer you'd like them.

measurements.name: Crotch depth (seated)
measurements.why: The key measurement for pants that don't pull or sag.
how: Sit up straight on a hard, flat chair.
Measure at your side from the waist elastic straight down to the chair seat.
Use a ruler held upright if the tape bends.
